messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify minValueNode returns the root when the tree has only one node (no left child).
test_metadata.rationale: Tests the minimal non-NULL input, ensuring the function correctly returns the input node when no left subtree exists. Catches off-by-one or improper loop exit bugs.

path_conditions: Input node's left child is NULL

assertions.name: assert_int_equal
assertions.purpose: Verify returned node's key matches the input node's key
assertions.usage: Check that the returned node is the same as the input node by key

assertions.name: assert_pointer_equal
assertions.purpose: Verify returned pointer is the same as input node pointer
assertions.usage: Check that the returned node pointer is identical to the input

utilities.name: helper_free_tree
utilities.purpose: Frees all nodes in the tree

data_structures: struct node (single node, left = NULL, right = NULL)
preconditions: Node's left and right pointers are NULL
setup_requirements.initial_state: A single-node tree (root only, no children)

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Pointer to a single node (no left child)
primary_function_args.concrete_value: pointer to node with key=17, left=NULL, right=NULL
primary_function_args.rationale: Triggers the path where the loop is not entered and the input node is returned

return_value.description: Pointer to the same node as input
return_value.validation: Returned pointer equals input pointer; returned key equals input key

side_effects.effect: No modification to input node or tree

state_changes: No change: single-node tree remains unchanged

assertions_required.description: Verify returned pointer is the same as the input node
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Function did not return the correct node

assertions_required.description: Verify returned node's key matches input node's key
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Returned node is not the correct node

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All memory freed, no resource leaks

operation_sequence: Allocate and initialize single node (key=17, left=NULL, right=NULL)
edge_cases_to_note: Do not pass NULL (that is a different path)
Do not add left child (would enter loop)

path_coverage_analysis.description: Input node is not NULL and has no left child; function returns input node

integration_test_suggestions: Test minValueNode on a multi-level tree to ensure it traverses left children
Test minValueNode with NULL input (should return NULL)
